parts.visual:
A massive part of a CEO's job is not fighting competitors, but fighting the government.

The Political Machine:
1. Lobbying: Hiring experts to legally persuade politicians to write laws that favor your company.
2. Regulatory Capture: When an industry becomes so powerful that it essentially controls the government agency meant to regulate it.
3. The Revolving Door: Hiring former government regulators to work as executives at your company.
parts.audio: Executives don't just follow the rules; they try to write them. Lobbying is the legal process of persuading politicians to pass laws that benefit your industry.

questions.question: Your tech company relies on importing cheap microchips. Congress is about to pass a massive tax on imported chips. What is your executive response?
options: Deploy 'Lobbyists' to Washington D.C. immediately to educate politicians on why this tax will destroy American jobs.
questions.correct_answer: Deploy 'Lobbyists' to Washington D.C. immediately to educate politicians on why this tax will destroy American jobs.
questions.explanation: Lobbying is how corporations defend their profit margins against political shifts. You must play the game.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO. What controversial practice is he using?
questions.tts_text: The head of the Federal Aviation Agency is retiring next month. Offer him a $2 million salary to be our new VP of Compliance.
questions.explanation: Hiring the people who used to regulate you gives you unparalleled access and influence over the regulatory agencies.

questions.question: Why do tech giants spend tens of millions of dollars a year on 'Government Relations'?
options: Because they have too much money.
Because a single new law (like banning a specific algorithm or mandating data localization) can wipe out billions of dollars in market cap overnight.
questions.correct_answer: Because a single new law (like banning a specific algorithm or mandating data localization) can wipe out billions of dollars in market cap overnight.
questions.explanation: Government Relations is an insurance policy against existential political threats.

questions.question: What is 'Regulatory Capture'?
options: When the police catch a criminal.
When a regulatory agency (like the FDA or EPA) becomes dominated by the very industries it is supposed to be regulating, acting in the industry's interest rather than the public's.
questions.correct_answer: When a regulatory agency (like the FDA or EPA) becomes dominated by the very industries it is supposed to be regulating, acting in the industry's interest rather than the public's.
questions.explanation: This is the ultimate (though highly controversial) victory for corporate lobbying.

pairs.match: Seeking to influence a politician or public official on an issue
The movement of personnel between roles as legislators and regulators
When an agency advances the commercial/political concerns of an industry
